what: The door widget plays keyframe animations on every guest press: a 450ms slide from translateX(-30px), then a 700ms verdict that sits invisible for 40% of its run and enters from scale(0.6). This breaks the 300ms UI budget and the 0.9-0.97 entrance scale. Pressing quickly restarts the keyframes from zero, and 18 chips invite quick presses.
evidence: assets/ext/js-ch5.css:111-114 `@keyframes door-in { 0% { transform: translateX(-30px); opacity: 0 } }`, `@keyframes door-verdict { 0%, 40% { transform: scale(0.6); opacity: 0 } }`, `.motion .door-stage.run .door-guest { animation: door-in 450ms ease-out 1 }`, `.door-verdict { animation: door-verdict 700ms ease-out 1 }`. Measured with getAnimations(): 450ms and 700ms. Reduced motion and 'Animations: off' correctly stop it (js-ch5.js:147 checks L.motionOn()). Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-1-5/a5/w390-029-p18.png
fix: Before → After (why): `door-in 450ms ease-out`, from `translateX(-30px)` → `door-in var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) both`, from `translateX(-12px); opacity: 0` (fired tens of times per visit, so it must stay short) · `door-verdict 700ms ease-out`, `0%,40% { scale(0.6) }` → `door-verdict var(--dur-ui) var(--ease-out) 120ms both`, from `scale(0.95); opacity: 0` (two short steps instead of a 700ms wait; nothing enters from near nothing).

what: On every chip press the rounding lanes draw their arrows with a 380ms stroke transition and a 90ms stagger per lane, so the fourth arrow finishes 650ms after the press. The transition uses the built-in `ease-out` instead of the token curve.
evidence: assets/ext/js-ch3.js:91 `arrow.style.transition = "stroke-dashoffset 380ms ease-out " + (k * 90) + "ms"`. Measured at 390: transitions 380ms with delays 0/90/180/270ms. It correctly checks L.motionOn() (:88). Crop: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-1-5/a3/w390-073-p42.png
fix: Before → After (why): `stroke-dashoffset 380ms ease-out` + `k * 90ms` → `stroke-dashoffset 200ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)` + `k * 40ms` (last arrow done by 320ms; the stagger belongs in Emil's 30-80ms band, and the strong curve matches the engine's --ease-out).

what: The bead bench's raised bead eases with `transition: transform 0.2s`, which uses the browser's default `ease` instead of the design tokens.

panel: ch1 P28, ch2 P25 (any readlist item wrapped in <span>)
what: The latest readlist rule sets `overflow-wrap: break-word` on inline code, although its comment says these keep `anywhere`. break-word doesn't lower min-content, and every JS readlist item wraps its text in a `<span>` grid item (min-width: auto). So a long token widens the span past the panel and gets clipped: `node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1607` overflows by 66px in ch1 P28, and `file:///…/unexpected_token.js:2` by 9px in ch2 P25. visual-rs-26-29 reported the same symptom; these are JS cases.
evidence: comic-widgets.css:410-412: comment '…Those keep `anywhere`' and then `:is(.readlist li, .checklist li) :is(code, samp) { display: inline; overflow-wrap: break-word; … }`. `<li><span>` count: ch1 24, ch2 34, ch3 14, ch4 66, ch5 27. Crops: /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-1-5/a1/w390-048-p28.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/7f030446-3270-51d4-abc1-d3638614f9af/scratchpad/review-visual-js-1-5/a2/w390-043-p25.png
fix: Before → After (why): `overflow-wrap: break-word` → `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (keep `display: inline`; anywhere lets the long token break when it must, so the column can shrink) · and add `.readlist li > * { min-width: 0 }` (a grid item shouldn't be wider than its 1fr track).
